vintage: Survey October 5 to November 6, 2005; report released February 21, 2006
table: Living Closer to Parents Means More Contact (p. 20); Most Families Not So Spread Out (p. 4); More Frequent Contact with Parents Who Live Out-of-Town (p. 4)
title: As Family Forms Change, Bonds Remain Strong: Families Drawn Together By Communication Revolution
universe: U.S. adults with at least one living parent (1,875 respondents); proximity to an adult child for parents with a financially independent child 18 and over (1,304)
limits: Contact means seeing or talking to a parent, so calls count with visits; the table compares a parent in the respondent's house, in the same town, or out of town, not counties or travel times. Out of town covers every distance from the next town to across the country. No contact figures are given by travel time; the proximity table gives only where parents live. A travel-time decay study was looked for: the INED (France) contact-by-travel-time paper named in a search was not reachable (ined.fr connect_rejected through the proxy), and no U.S. table of contact by travel time was found. The frequency codes used to turn the contact distribution into contacts a year (daily 365, weekly or more 52, monthly or more 12, several times a year 4, once a year 1, less often 0) are this file's conversion, not Pew's.
